verified.exploit_entry_point: The CMS front end: a Theme is loaded, a Cms\Classes\Controller is constructed and Controller::run(url) renders the page and its layout (the project's own ControllerTest drives the same entry point). Every security case writes its own temporary theme and renders through it; the write route is observed with a second render in a fresh PHP process, as a later request would be.

routes: T1: a template expression registers a dynamic method on the page object (mixed-case spelling and the attribute() helper too) or on the layout object, then invokes it with an arbitrary PHP function
T2: a template expression binds an event on the page object or on the page controller (both bindEvent and bindEventOnce), then fires it
T3: a template expression reaches the page's storage builder and writes a PHP code section into its own template file; a later request renders it
T4 (coupled, functional): legitimate expressions, filters, loops, partials, deployed code sections, PHP-side event binding and the storage API keep working
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own CMS unit suite (tests/unit/cms, 94 tests, 460 assertions) passes in the image at the pinned commit and runs as part of the functional group, together with 7 functional cases written for this task; 101 functional tests in total.

traps.shape: The objects a CMS template can reach expose the framework's own extension mechanism: a template expression can register an arbitrary callable under a new name and then invoke it, so the template runs any PHP function. The same holds for the layout object, for a mixed-case spelling of the registering method, and through the framework's own attribute helper.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The shipped safe-mode message says only editing of the PHP code section is disabled, so template markup looks like presentation and the objects it can reach look like ordinary view data.
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-94vp-rmqv-5875) at the pinned commit; fixed upstream by 4c650bb775ab

traps.shape: The event mechanism is a second way to turn template content into a call: bind an attacker-chosen callable as a listener on the page object or on the page controller, then fire the event with attacker-chosen arguments. A rule written for the registering methods leaves it open.
traps.where: src/Support/Traits/Emitter.php:30 (bindEvent), src/Support/Traits/Emitter.php:41 (bindEventOnce), src/Support/Traits/Emitter.php:108 (fireEvent) in october/rain 1.0.467; reached from modules/cms/classes/Controller.php:610
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Event binding is an application-programming API used by components and plugins, so it reads as trusted developer surface rather than something template content can use.
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-r89v-cgv7-3jhx), the bypass fixed by d34fb8ab5110; real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: The storage layer behind a page is reachable from a template expression, so a template can write a PHP code section into its own file straight through the datasource, bypassing the save-time guard. The check has to hold for where content ends up, not only for what a render does right now.
traps.where: src/Halcyon/Builder.php:382 (update) and src/Halcyon/Builder.php:367/398 (insert/delete) in october/rain 1.0.467; modules/cms/classes/CmsCompoundObject.php:145 (the save-time guard that this path never runs)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: A guard written for method calls on the objects a template uses never inspects the storage writer, and the write is a data change rather than an obvious code-execution primitive.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: upstream added the storage-writing method names to the same policy later (ea67b615e, 2020-12-18), untouched by both published fixes for these advisories
